_readme: THE SHARED-SERVER REGISTER — [pipeline B-1] company/pipeline/04-backend-platform.md
The complete set of capabilities the ONE shared `platform` Worker provides — every ROUTE it mounts
and every BINDING any Worker in this repo declares — together with what each one is FOR, who calls
or reads it, and whether it is authenticated.
WHY IT EXISTS. There is exactly one `platform` Worker and one `platform_db` behind the whole
portfolio, so a defect here is not one app's bug — it is every app's outage, including apps that do
not exist yet. SIX other stage-4 requirements quantify over 'the shared capability set' or 'every
binding', and until this file landed that set did not exist. An undefined right-hand side cannot
reject anything, so all six reported clean over nothing:
[4]B-2   onboarding an app is DATA, not a source edit    -> the route set this must not change
[4]B-3   the server can authenticate a caller            -> auth: required must be non-zero
[4]B-4a  every written row belongs to a registered app   -> the write routes, enumerated
[4]B-13  no unauthenticated route can be made expensive  -> auth: public x limiter, below
[4]B-14  every field of every shared route is pinned     -> the route count is the pair floor
[4]B-18  one shared bucket, every bucket has a reader    -> bindings[], and its reader limb
🔴 THE ONE RULE THAT MAKES THIS FILE MEAN ANYTHING: MEMBERSHIP IS NOT A CLAIM, RESOLUTION IS.
Writing `"client": "TBD"` was the original acceptance criterion's third limb, and a string field is
satisfied by any string. Every `client` here is an EXPRESSION that must appear in comment-stripped
source in a file OUTSIDE the serving Worker, and must itself contain the route's own static path —
so a client entry cannot be satisfied by the server's own declaration of the route, and cannot
survive the route being renamed. `_registerInWorkspace` matched its own declaration six times in
this repo; this is the seventh place that was not allowed to happen.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-platform-register.mjs:
· LIMB 1 route set == what services/platform/src/index.ts MOUNTS, parsed (following app.route()
into each sub-router), in BOTH directions                                            [B-1]
· LIMB 2 a route with no client is NOT a build failure — it PRINTS its `unconsumedReason` on
every run, and the reason must be non-empty. Same shape as
assert-capability-register.mjs's zero-consumer rule                                   [B-1]
· LIMB 3 binding set == every `d1_databases`/`kv_namespaces`/`r2_buckets`/`ratelimits` entry
across services/*/wrangler.jsonc AND the brick template, in BOTH directions; each must have a
REAL READER — `env.<BINDING>` in comment-stripped code in a file that is NOT the Env type
declaration                                                                    [B-1, B-18]
· LIMB 4 every `auth: public` route reaches withinRateLimit/withinEdgeCeiling at a real call site
in its owningFile, or declares a `noLimiterReason` that prints on every run          [B-13]
⚠️ COVERAGE IS A RELATIONSHIP, NEVER A NUMBER. The route floor is 'equals what index.ts mounts' and
the binding floor is 'equals what the wrangler configs declare' — both derived from files CI already
parses. There is no tuned integer anyone can lower. The one integer in the guard is a self-check
that the PARSE still finds routes at all, because a parser that matches nothing reports perfect
agreement with an empty register.
⚠️ NOT tooling/capability-register.json. That file is the PACKAGE register (stage 2/3): Dart
packages, seams and their consumers. This one is the SERVER's. They are deliberately separate files
because they answer to different guards, different stages and different trees — merging them would
make one guard's coverage floor depend on the other's subject.

_why: The Worker whose mounted routes the register's `routes` array must equal, exactly. Named as data
rather than hardcoded in the guard so that the guard fails loudly if this Worker is renamed or
moved, instead of quietly scanning a path that no longer exists.
servingWorker.name: platform

_why: Every config whose bindings the register must account for. DERIVED at runtime by globbing
services/*/wrangler.jsonc plus the brick's service template — this list is the guard's COVERAGE
assertion, not its input: if the glob finds a config that is not named here, or names one the
glob cannot find, the scan and the tree have diverged and the build fails.
The brick template is IN SCOPE on purpose. assert-clone-contract.mjs inspects only the throwaway
CI probe stamp, so services/subly-api is invisible to it — which is exactly how a per-app R2
bucket stayed live from 2026-07-17 with every guard green.

routes.purpose: Deploy verification. Answers `{ ok, app, version, time }` from vars — no I/O at all.
routes.unconsumedReason: 🔄 CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — IT HAS A MACHINE CONSUMER AND HAS FOR SOME TIME. `tooling/ops/post-deploy-smoke.mjs` fetches this route from `deploy-workers.yml` (twice, both Workers) and joins the deploy to a build through the `build` field; `deploy-web.yml` smokes it too. The previous text — "no programmatic client by design … the honest state is zero clients" — was true when written and false at head, and it PRINTED GREEN every run because limb 2 only reports unconsumed reasons rather than checking them. [4]B-14 now pins the field set the smoke joins on.
routes.noLimiterReason: It does NO I/O — no D1 query, no KV read, no subrequest — so there is nothing an attacker can make expensive beyond the Worker invocation itself, which the account-wide request ceiling already bounds. A limiter here would spend a Rate Limiting namespace (Free tier is finite) to protect a constant-time JSON literal. [4]B-13

routes.purpose: CFG-1 runtime config: compiled-in defaults overlaid with a KV override (`config:<app>`), edge-cached 300s. DATA and flags only, never server-driven UI, never secrets.

client.note: The URL the transport actually builds, at the assignment — not the doc comment three lines above it, which says the same thing and is stripped before matching.

routes.purpose: G-12 first-party analytics ingest ([ADR 011]). Batched, pseudonymous, consent-gated CLIENT-side. Unauthenticated deliberately: the most valuable events (first_launch, paywall_viewed) happen before any login exists, and a bearer token would attach an identity to rows whose whole point is that they carry none.

client.note: The first positional argument of the real `_dio.post` call.

routes.purpose: The DPDP consent artifact each analytics event references. Append-only: a withdrawal is a NEW row with granted=0, never an UPDATE, because the audit trail is the point (DPDP §6(3)).

client.note: The first positional argument of the real `_dio.post` call.

routes.purpose: G2 in-app account deletion ([4]B-5). THE FIRST `auth: required` ROUTE ON THIS WORKER, and the reason src/middleware/auth.ts is not a dead file. Three limbs: every user-owned table in platform_db (DERIVED from the schema — a `user_id` column is the selector — not from a literal array somebody must remember to extend), then the identity record itself. Refuses 501 while SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is unset, so it ships honest rather than not at all.
routes.unconsumedReason: 🔄 CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — THE CLIENT HALF EXISTS. `packages/core/lib/src/auth/account_deletion.dart` models the three refusals this route answers with, `packages/auth_supabase/lib/src/supabase_auth_repository.dart:43` calls `DELETE /v1/account`, and `packages/core/test/account_deletion_test.dart` covers the 501. The claim that it was "blocked on stage 2" was true when written and false at head. [4]B-14 pins the STATUS SET rather than a body, because this route's client reads no body key — `AccountDeletionFailure.forStatus` is the contract.

routes.purpose: [pipeline 5]M-4 — ANY app reads ITS entitlement from the host every stamped app already has. The brick's DEFAULT stamp is CLIENT-ONLY ([ADR 020]), so until this route existed the only working entitlement read in the repo was inside services/subly-api — i.e. inside the one legacy app that happens to have a backend, while every app the factory stamps had no way to ask whether its user had paid. Scoped by BOTH user_id (from the verified token) AND app_id (a required query parameter that must name a registered app); the money boundary fails closed on every undecidable case, including a row whose money environment is not this deploy's ([5]M-12).
routes.unconsumedReason: 🔄 CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — THERE IS A DART CLIENT. `packages/api_client/lib/src/dio_entitlement_transport.dart:40` issues `GET {platformBaseUrl}/v1/entitlements?app_id=<id>` as a `core.EntitlementTransport`. The claim of "no Dart client yet … nothing fetches" was true when written and false at head. [4]B-14 pins the three envelope keys plus the ten-key row item.
routes.noLimiterReason: NOT APPLICABLE — `auth: required`, so limb 4 does not range over it. Recorded anyway because the read is on a launch path and the 100k Worker-requests/day Free ceiling is ACCOUNT-WIDE across ~50 apps: this must never become a per-screen fetch, which is a client-side constraint the cache in packages/core exists to satisfy.

routes.purpose: [pipeline 5]M-9 — the user-initiated cancel path. Mounted behind app.use('/v1/plan/*', platformAuth), so the subscription is resolved from the VERIFIED SESSION and never from the request body; the body carries only app_id. Writes an append-only cancellation_requests row (migration 0005) rather than mutating entitlements in place, so a cancel is a fact with a timestamp instead of a state change that loses its own history. 202 is a success and the common case: the host records the request and answers 202 when it could not also execute it against the merchant of record synchronously.

client.note: The URL the transport actually builds, at the post() call site — not the doc comment on line 5, which names the same path and is stripped before matching.

routes.purpose: [pipeline 5]M-1 — the ONE door a merchant of record knocks on. Verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the RAW body with the rail's per-destination secret, records the notification verbatim exactly once, acks, then derives the entitlement. [ADR 020]:18 puts it on the SHARED host because a per-app Worker must never see a webhook: fifty stamped apps inherit one verified rail rather than fifty copies of a signature check. [ADR 004] fixes the merchant of record as Paddle / Lemon Squeezy; the adapter registry is what makes the choice a config change.
routes.unconsumedReason: NO CLIENT IN THIS REPO, BY CONSTRUCTION — the caller is the merchant of record's own delivery system, not any code we ship. This is the one route whose 'who calls it' answer is a vendor, and the honest state is zero in-tree clients. What replaces the client check for this route is tooling/ci/assert-mor-adapters.mjs, which asserts the verifier exists, is CALLED, and is the only path to an entitlements write across ALL of services/**.
routes.noLimiterReason: It DOES reach withinEdgeCeiling (MONEY_CEILING_LIMITER) — this field is present only to record why the ceiling is the server-derived one and not the fairness bucket: there is no per-install identity on a webhook to be fair between, and the only meaningful key is one the caller cannot choose.

routes.purpose: The Paddle CREATE-TRANSACTION server half ([ADR 044]). Creates a DRAFT transaction from `items` alone and returns its `checkout.url`. 🔴 THE SHAPE IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY: the create body type carries NO settable `status` field at all, so passing `status:"billed"` is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a code-review catch. That matters because `billed` mints an invoice number and an immutable tax record, and on a cardless trial Paddle auto-completes the transaction and creates a subscription — removing the human from a loop everything else here assumes.
routes.unconsumedReason: ⚠️ NOTHING CALLS THIS ROUTE TODAY, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DRESSED UP. [ADR 044] §5(2) found that `Paddle.Checkout.open({items})` opens a checkout with NO server-created transaction and NO API key on the request path, exercising the identical payment-link and `_ptxn` machinery — "the server endpoint is therefore not a v1 dependency, which was the load-bearing surprise of this investigation". The owner then chose BOTH rungs, so this exists as rung 2. It earns its place the moment a transaction needs something the overlay cannot pre-fill: a known `customer_id`, a discount, or `custom_data` carrying our own account id — and §6 records that last one as a FILED DEFECT, not a nicety. Until then this is an UNCONSUMED route by design, and the honest state is zero clients.

bindings.purpose: The ONE entitlements + analytics + consent database for the whole portfolio. services/platform is the SOLE migrations applier; every other Worker binds it without a migrations_dir.

Subly's own database, bound into `platform` READ/WRITE for the nightly renewals fan-out only. ⚠️ This binding is the thing that does NOT scale: a 50-app portfolio cannot carry 50 hand-added D1 bindings on one Worker. Recorded here so the next app's stamp meets the ceiling as a known cost rather than as a surprise ([4]B-11 derives the job set; the fan-out target list is still `appTargets()`'s hardcoded array).

A stamped app's own private database — the only datastore an opt-in backend owns outright. D1 Free is 10 databases per account and platform_db is one of them, which is why a backend is opt-in rather than default ([ADR 020]).
Per-app CFG-1 config overrides, keyed `config:<app>`, read on the launch path of every app and edge-cached for 300s.
Caches the Supabase JWKS document so an ES256 verify does not fetch it per request. One identity project portfolio-wide, so one cache.

FAIRNESS bucket for /v1/events + /v1/consent, keyed `(app_id, anon_id)`. ⚠️ That key is ENTIRELY client-chosen on a route that is unauthenticated by design, so it bounds one honest install and nothing more — EVENTS_CEILING_LIMITER is the half a caller cannot rotate out of.
SERVER-DERIVED ceiling for /v1/events + /v1/consent, keyed `edge:<colo>:<asn>` from `request.cf` — no request-body value is in the key. Its own namespace so it cannot spend the fairness budget.

The same server-derived ceiling for GET /config/:app — the other unauthenticated route on this Worker that does I/O. Its own namespace so config traffic and analytics traffic cannot exhaust each other.

The server-derived ceiling for POST /v1/money/:provider, keyed `edge:<colo>:<asn>`. Its OWN namespace so a flood of forged notifications cannot exhaust the budget analytics ingest and config resolution depend on — both of those are on every app's LAUNCH path, so borrowing from them would let anyone who finds this URL degrade the whole portfolio.
